The boxes group the export subpaths by function; the reference index documents each subpath.
Section heading.
A site declares one adapter, typically at src/theme/cairn.config.ts, listing concepts, repo, sender, render, and optional seams.
The engine hard-codes no concept, directory, or field; every factory, screen, and helper reads the one adapter.
Left at scaffold defaults the adapter yields an owner and editor CMS.
Adding concepts, roles, or screens edits the adapter rather than forking the engine.
The root barrel and the SvelteKit layer are the core and kit split the diagram draws.
The root barrel has no SvelteKit import and the SvelteKit subpath has no Svelte component; components sit on admin and public.
The split keeps the content model usable from a build script and the route layer free of Svelte's client runtime.
Each seam is a typed contract the engine consumes; sites supply them rather than reach into internals.
The content map holds one ConceptConfig per concept, each with a fieldset.
One render function, built with createRenderer and a registry, serves the live preview and every public page.
The access map and role vocabulary gate route authorization and nav visibility from one declaration.
navLayout is one ordered tree arranging the whole sidebar, mixing engine and custom screens.
The Backend is the read-and-commit interface; createGithubApp is the only shipped provider.
AssetConfig resolves into the R2 binding and upload limits that routes and the media library read.
Section heading.
A save never touches the default branch directly.
Sequence diagram title and the framing of a save and publish path.
A save commits with the editor as author and cairn-cms[bot] as committer.
Saves land on a per-entry branch; publishing copies it to the default branch, which triggers the deploy.
Diagram participants and the editor saving an entry.
The commit carries editor as author and cairn-cms[bot] as committer.
The holding branch receives the commit; publish copies it to the default branch, which triggers deploy.
The holding branch is per entry and named cairn/<concept>/<id>.
Multiple saves accumulate on the holding branch, and the admin lists pending entries from it.
Author is the editor and committer cairn-cms[bot], so history credits the editor and every commit traces to the App.
Pointers to the security model and content model pages.
Section heading.
One entry's full body, for a public page render or an edit load, is read directly through the Backend.
Corpus-wide needs such as an index, tag list, sitemap, or link check read the committed manifest.
The manifest is a JSON summary of each entry's identity, routing, and outgoing links.
The manifest is rebuilt at build time.
The manifest row is updated in the save commit.
The manifest exists so the admin and delivery layer never crawl the repository through the GitHub API.
The engine owns D1 for auth and R2 for media bytes directly; the data tiers page places the manifest.
Section heading.
Directive dispatch, commit tree operations, and the guard's CSRF and session resolution are engine-internal.
Internals sit behind stability-tiered public surfaces, so upgrades may change them while contracts hold.
An undocumented import signals site-owned work; a site's own domain reaches the engine only via seams.
